prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a top-down egocentric view of the camera wearer squatting on the ground facing downward toward a patch of leafy green plants, with no other people present and no one looking toward the camera. The camera wearer's bent left and right knees at the bottom edge are the nearest surfaces at roughly 0.3 to 0.4 metres, while their left and right hands (~0.1 to 0.3 metres apart) reach forward at 0.4 to 0.5 metres above the soil (~0.6 to 0.8 metres away), alongside a curved sickle blade and a small metal bowl on the right that are all within arm's reach. Across frames 1 to 4, the right hand moves from the harvested bundle at bottom-centre toward the metal bowl on the right and back, before the camera tilts slightly upward and left in frame 5, shifting the right knee and bowl mostly out of view while the left hand partially occludes the sickle and soil below it. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates the vertical layering of individual upper plant leaves (brighter, ~0.4 to 0.5 metres) from the lower leaves and recessed soil underneath, which blend together in colour and shadow. However, the depth map is unreliable because it assigns bright near-depth values to sunlit upper leaves in the upper half so they appear as close as the wearer's knees (~0.3 to 0.4 metres), while rendering shadowed soil pockets in frames 3 and 4 as pitch-black infinite depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only the foreground elements at the bottom of the downward-facing scene—specifically the camera wearer's limbs and the small metal container—while leaving the entire upper bed of leafy plants, soil, and sickle unlabelled in black. Within arm's reach at the bottom edge (roughly 0.3 to 0.6 metres from the head-mounted camera), the wearer's left knee/leg and left arm on the left and right hand/leg on the right are segmented at ~0.1 to 0.3 metres from each other, with the container (labelled 'bowl' in frames 1–2 and 'cup' in frame 3) positioned immediately above and in front of the right leg at ~0.6 metres; no other people are present. Across the five frames, the right-side 'person' mask shifts rightward into the bowl in frame 3 (partially occluding the container) and returns toward the centre in frame 4, while all masks disappear completely in frame 5 when the camera tilts upward and left, leaving the lower limbs only partly in view at the bottom border. The segmentation map highlights the exact boundary between the wearer's skin and the adjacent metal bowl in frames 1 to 3, which is somewhat visually cluttered against the soil and chopped greens in the RGB image. However, it is highly unreliable because it fragments the single camera wearer into two or three separate 'person' instances (splitting the left leg/arm from the right arm/leg), switches the metal bowl's class to 'cup' in frame 3, misses the bowl when occluded in frame 4, and fails to detect any body parts or objects at all in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is almost entirely black across the five frames, detecting no yellow body skeleton for the downward-facing camera wearer (whose torso and head are out of view behind the camera) and confirming no other people are present or facing the camera wearer. It renders only a single magenta 2D hand skeleton for the camera wearer's right hand within arm's reach (~0.4 to 0.5 metres from the camera) in the lower-central region of frame 2 and the lower-right region of frame 3. Between frames 2 and 3, this detected right hand shifts roughly 0.2 metres to the right and slightly upward to reach into the metal bowl (~0.6 metres from the camera and ~0.2 metres right of the left hand), with fingers angled downward and leftward before disappearing in frames 4 and 5 as the camera turns slightly upward. Where present in frames 2 and 3, the magenta wireframe reveals the precise articulation and flexion of the right thumb and fingers even where they overlap and self-occlude over the plant stems and bowl rim in the RGB image. Nevertheless, the pose map is largely unreliable because it completely misses the wearer's visible left hand holding the greens in all five frames, misses the right hand in frames 1, 4, and 5, and fails to track the visible lower legs at the bottom boundary.
